findings.title: Concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key are no longer serialized
findings.body: BuildIndex no longer holds cacheMu while creating and populating the index; it only locks for the final cache assignment. Because GetIndex returns nil until that assignment, two concurrent getOrCreateIndex/Search calls for the same NamespacedResource can both build an index. For file-backed indexes both call bleve.New on the same directory, so one can fail or contend on the on-disk index; for memory indexes both build fully and the later assignment overwrites and leaks the earlier unclosed index. Add per-key synchronization/singleflight or a double-checked cache lookup so only one build per key runs while different keys still build in parallel.

findings.title: Search init workers race on shared err and counter
findings.body: Every errgroup closure in init assigns to the same outer err variable and increments totalBatchesIndexed without synchronization. Concurrent workers therefore data-race, and a failing build's error can be overwritten by a concurrent successful build before the failing closure returns it, letting startup proceed with a missing index and producing incorrect span counts. Use a closure-local err returned directly to errgroup and an atomic or mutex-protected counter.

findings.title: Handlers no longer reject requests after Stop
findings.body: All RPC handlers removed their s.Init(ctx) check, but Stop relies on mutating s.initErr to make subsequent Init calls return the stopping/stopped error. Create and the other handlers never consult initErr now, and they use the request context rather than the cancelled server context, so direct in-process callers can still read, write, delete, search, or use blobs after lifecycle Stop instead of failing fast. Keep a lightweight stopped/init-state check in handlers, separate from the sync.Once initialization.

findings.title: Constructor returns no handle to clean up partially initialized services on Init failure
findings.body: If s.Init fails after lifecycle initialization or after search.init has started its background watch goroutine, NewResourceServer returns nil without calling cancel or lifecycle Stop. The caller receives no server handle with which to clean up, so the opened backend and the search watch/poller (which uses context.Background) can keep running and repeated construction attempts can accumulate pollers. On Init error, stop/cancel whatever was started before returning the original error.

findings.title: TotalDocs iterates the index cache without holding cacheMu
findings.body: TotalDocs ranges over b.cache without RLock while BuildIndex now inserts into that map under a short Lock at the end of a build. Concurrent index creation (for example from the search watch goroutine handling a new namespace while init logs TotalDocs, or later lazy builds) can therefore race with this iteration, which the race detector flags and Go can turn into a fatal concurrent-map-iteration/write panic. Hold cacheMu.RLock for the iteration.
